problems.q: What is the molecular shape of NH3? Nitrogen has three bonds and one lone pair.
problems.why: Four electron groups arrange as a tetrahedron. One group is a lone pair, so the shape made by the atoms is trigonal pyramidal. OpenStax AF2e §4.6.
hints: Name the shape from the atoms only. The lone pair still pushes the bonds into a pyramid.

problems.q: CO2 is a linear molecule and the two C–O bonds pull in opposite directions. Is the molecule polar or nonpolar?
problems.why: Each C–O bond is polar, but the two pulls are equal and opposite in a straight line. They cancel, so CO2 is nonpolar. OpenStax AF2e §4.6.
hints: A polar bond does not always make a polar molecule. Check whether the bond pulls cancel.

problems.q: The electronegativity difference for a C–F bond is 1.43. A difference below 0.4 is treated as nonpolar covalent. Is the C–F bond polar covalent or nonpolar covalent?
problems.why: 1.43 is greater than 0.4, and the atoms still share electrons. The bond is polar covalent. OpenStax AF2e §4.2.
hints: Compare 1.43 with 0.4. Sharing is still covalent; the size of the difference decides polar or nonpolar.
